about: More of sedi-1's verifier layer (test-plan item 6): registry evidence, revocation through a chain, seals, edge SAIDs and operator shapes. Each fixture is a bundle in the form acdc_build reads; each case names the sedi-1 choices its verdict rests on and its security triage, and lists every finding the sedi-1 model makes. The verdict itself is the model's (generators/spec_tables/sedi_cases.py).

cases.title: Three issued updates
cases.description: A credential whose registry carries three updates at n=1, 2 and 3, each anchored in the issuer's KEL; the head, n=3, records it issued. A sedi-1 verifier should find it valid.

cases.title: Later updates withheld, their seals in the KEL
cases.description: As SL-01, but the bundle withholds the updates at n=2 and n=3, while the issuer's KEL still anchors them. The verifier holds the n=1 state and knows later state exists that it cannot see. A sedi-1 verifier should find it incomplete.
cases.triage: Accepting it lets a holder present an old state by withholding the updates after it.

cases.title: Update anchored past the KEL's end
cases.description: As SC-01 (two issued updates), but the bundle's KEL for the issuer stops before the interaction event that anchors the n=2 update, so the verifier cannot see that update anchored. A sedi-1 verifier should find it incomplete.
cases.triage: Accepting it accepts a registry state whose anchor the verifier never saw.

cases.title: Two-hop chain
cases.description: N, issued by I to H, has an I2I edge to F, issued by Q to I, which has an I2I edge to G, issued by R to Q. A sedi-1 verifier should find it valid.

cases.title: Revoked middle node of a two-hop chain
cases.description: As SL-04, but F, the middle node, is revoked. Validity is chain-strict, so N is not valid. A sedi-1 verifier should find it invalid.
cases.triage: Accepting it lets authority flow through a revoked credential.

cases.title: Seal whose d does not match
cases.description: As SV-01, but the event seal anchoring the n=1 update carries a d that is not that update's SAID, so nothing in the KEL anchors the update. A sedi-1 verifier should find it incomplete.
cases.triage: Accepting it accepts a registry update its issuer never anchored.

cases.title: Edge whose d is wrong
cases.description: As SV-10, but the edge block's d is changed after issuance to a digest that is not the SAID of the block, so the block's SAID does not verify. A sedi-1 verifier should find it invalid.
cases.triage: Accepting it accepts an edge that commits to nothing.

cases.title: Edge whose d is the far node's SAID
cases.description: As SV-10, but the edge block's d is changed after issuance to the far node's SAID, which is not the block's own, so the block's SAID does not verify. A sedi-1 verifier should find it invalid.
cases.triage: Accepting it accepts an edge that commits to nothing.

cases.title: Unknown member in an operator list
cases.description: As SV-10, but the edge's o is ["I2I", "XYZ"], which sedi-1 cannot evaluate. A sedi-1 verifier should find it incomplete.
cases.triage: Accepting it applies a weaker rule than the issuer wrote.

cases.title: Operator list with a number
cases.description: As SV-10, but the edge's o is [1], which sedi-1 cannot evaluate. A sedi-1 verifier should find it incomplete.
cases.triage: Accepting it applies a weaker rule than the issuer wrote.

cases.title: Operator as an object
cases.description: As SV-10, but the edge's o is {"op": "I2I"}, which sedi-1 cannot evaluate. A sedi-1 verifier should find it incomplete.
cases.triage: Accepting it applies a weaker rule than the issuer wrote.

cases.title: AND group with one edge
cases.description: N, issued by I to H, has an edge group g with the operator AND holding one I2I edge to F, issued by Q to I. A sedi-1 verifier should find it valid.

cases.title: Empty AND group
cases.description: N, issued by I to H, has an edge group g with the operator AND and no members. sedi-1 treats an empty group as malformed. A sedi-1 verifier should find it invalid.
cases.triage: Accepting it lets an empty group stand in for the edges the issuer required.

cases.title: Empty OR group
cases.description: N, issued by I to H, has an edge group g with the operator OR and no members. sedi-1 treats an empty group as malformed. A sedi-1 verifier should find it invalid.
cases.triage: Accepting it lets an empty group stand in for the edges the issuer required.
